items.text: Oil jumped to $98 on Red Sea attacks, with WTI +4.9% and Brent +3.9% week-over-week. Geopolitical supply risk is real and driving near-term volatility, but the energy shock is not yet translating to broad-based CPI reacceleration—headline CPI at 3.46% YoY, down from 4.17% prior. Special-situations investors should monitor credit exposure to energy-heavy capex plans and refinancing schedules at indebted upstream/midstream operators.

Unemployment rate stands at a low 4.2%, and new applications for unemployment assistance are still at historically low levels. But payrolls printed at only +57K in June after +129K prior—a sharp sequential deceleration suggesting labor market cooling has begun. Fed funds at 3.75% with no cuts priced through year-end risk wage disinflation without employment loss, but risk to credit is asymmetric: weak payrolls could force Fed capitulation faster than consensus expects.

CPI headline declined to 3.46% from 4.17%, and core down to 2.57% from 2.82%. However, year-ahead inflation expectations inched down to a still-elevated 4.6% from 4.8% in May, while PCE readings show sticky core at 3.41% (vs 3.32% prior). Goods disinflation and energy moderation are real, but service-side wage pressures remain—a stubborn feature that constrains near-term rate cuts and supports spreads, but not infinitely.

ECB leaves deposit rate unchanged at 2.25%, as widely expected on July 23; the ECB left rates unchanged at its July 2026 meeting, with the deposit rate at 2.25%, as it monitors energy shocks and inflation. Fed on hold at 3.75%, and futures markets indicating roughly an 89% probability of no change. Central banks are paused, watching energy; rates will likely remain sticky above 3% through H2 absent a hard recession signal.

HY OAS +13 bps to 281 (tightest in weeks), IG OAS +3 bps to 81, CCC OAS +20 bps to 1001 bps. Curve flattening to 35 bps (from 36). High-yield spread tightening despite energy shock suggests investors are pricing resilience, but CCC-land is feeling stress—watch for covenant-light refinance rolls and distressed M&A targets; quality bifurcation will be key.

Resilient but cooling services expansion amid stable consumer spending and modest GDP growth projections near 2.0% for 2026. ISM Mfg at 53.3 in June (expansion 6 months running), Services PMI at 54.0 (down from 54.5). GDPNow at 1.54%, off from 1.24% prior—potential H2 stumble if labor rolls over further. Sub-2% growth with tight policy = compressed valuations for leveraged issuers reliant on volume growth.

The University of Michigan's widely watched Consumer Sentiment Index surged 10% this month to 54.4, from 49.5 in June. July's preliminary reading marked the second straight monthly boost and represented the highest level since February, driven by gasoline price relief. Yet mortgage rates at 6.58% (up 3 bps) and existing home sales YoY at -2.4% signal cooling demand. Housing starts rebounded to 1427K but affordability remains punitive—watch for HPA deceleration pressuring residential CMBS and home-builder leverage.

themeCards.title: Middle East Energy Shock
themeCards.statusLine: WTI +4.9% to 84.38, Brent +3.9% to 86.99 week-on-week on Red Sea attacks; oil jumped to $98 on Red Sea attacks. Supply risk real but not yet broad CPI reacceleration.
themeCards.relevance: Energy-heavy issuers facing input cost pressure and capex inflation; refiners and midstream under margin squeeze. CRE/leveraged ops exposed to rising utility costs. Credit markets pricing only modest duration risk—tail event if shock persists.

themeCards.title: Payroll Collapse Risk
themeCards.statusLine: June payrolls at +57K (consensus ~150K), down sharply from +129K prior. Labor market rolling over faster than consensus; unemployment at 4.2% but trend deteriorating.
themeCards.relevance: Triggers asymmetric risk for special situations: weak labor can force Fed cuts sooner than consensus (bullish for duration/credit), but also signals demand destruction (bearish for corporate leverage). Watch next print (July, release ~Aug 2) for confirmation.

themeCards.title: CCC Stress Widening
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS at 1001 bps (+20 bps this week), vs HY at 281 bps (+13). Quality bifurcation accelerating; covenant-light maturities facing refinance risk.
themeCards.relevance: High-impact for special situations: distressed M&A opportunity set expanding if spreads keep widening. Refinancing cliff for weak credits mid-H2. Opportunistic selector of CCC credits at sub-100 MOIC discount warrant close monitoring.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Inflation, Easing Fed Action
themeCards.statusLine: PCE core at 3.41% (up 9 bps); year-ahead inflation expectations sticky at 4.6%. Central banks on hold (Fed 3.75%, ECB 2.25%), data-dependent but energy-cautious.
themeCards.relevance: Constrains rate-cut duration. Supports spreads near-term but caps upside for duration plays. Low-growth + sticky inflation = compressed equity, wide credit, inverted curve—ideal for relative-value special situations, weak for gross leveraged longs.

themeCards.title: Housing Affordability Cliff
themeCards.statusLine: Mortgage rates 6.58% (up 3 bps), existing home sales YoY -2.4%, yet starts rebounded to 1427K. Affordability crisis persists despite rate stability and sentiment rebound.
themeCards.relevance: CMBS, residential debt, home-builder credit under pressure. Negative equity loops risk if HPA turns; construction leverage exposed to materials cost shock. Watch quarterly earnings for builder guidance on margin and volume trade-offs; refinance wall for 2025-26 maturities widening.

themeCards.title: China Growth Slowdown
themeCards.statusLine: Official June PMI at 50.3 (beat expectations but barely in expansion); private surveys show divergence and demand weakness. US tariff uncertainty and domestic stimulus lags.
themeCards.relevance: Demand shock for US exporters (autos, semiconductors, industrials); export credit margins pressuring corporate leverage in exposed sectors. Asia-focused supply chains and commodity credit at risk; watch China credit stress contagion risk if PMI drops below 50.

consensus.Payrolls: +150K to +170K exp (last print +57K June 1; large surprise downside risk)
consensus.PCE: Core PCE 3.2-3.3% YoY exp (last print 3.41% May 1)
consensus.PPI: +3.2% YoY exp (last print 5.51% June 1, declining trend)
consensus.Retail Sales: +0.3% to +0.4% m/m exp (last print +0.2% m/m June 1)
consensus.ISM Mfg: 52.5-53.0 exp (July, due Aug 3; last print 53.3 June 1)
consensus.ISM Services: 53.5-54.0 exp (July, due Aug 5; last print 54.0 June 1)

regime.label: Mid-Cycle Slowdown
regime.detail: Energy shock, cooling labor, sticky core inflation, central banks paused, HY spreads resilient but CCC widening, growth at 1.5-2%, floating-rate risk subsiding, credit selective.
